MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 14, 2023
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Goodell at 5:00 p.m., on February 14, 2023, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 9, 2023, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Ruesch
  Council Member Vasquez (arrived at 5:12 pm)
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 pm, Mayor Goodell recessed to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened
at 6:00 pm with all City Council Members present.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Vasquez

PRESENTATIONS

City Council Minutes  1  February 14, 2023
 P1. Congresswoman Young Kim

  Received introduction from Congresswoman Young Kim

P2. Recognize the 2022 Employees of the Year

  Mayor Goodell presented plaques to (1) Senior Public Services Supervisor Bryan Zahn, City
  of Mission Viejo Employee of the Year; (2) Fire Captain Danny Goodwin, Orange County
  Fire Authority Employee of the Year; and (3) Crime Prevention Specialist Timory
  McElwain, Orange County Sheriff's Department Employee of the Year.

P3. Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Goodell presented certificates of commendation to the "Marine of the Quarter" Lance
  Corporal Arandy Mendoza, and "Noncommissioned Officer of the Quarter" Sergeant
  Alexandra C. Munoz.

P4. 2022 State of the City

  Received presentation.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Mark Neely, M.V.: Spoke on policing, law and humanity on black people in this country.
Suggested the solution is related to money, and to start reducing a portion of the police pension.

Becky Butler, M.V.: Remarked on Consent Calendar Item #13, Ordinance 23-349. She stated the
unwillingness to include an anti-nepotism clause and the removal of Commission term limits is
unethical and embarrassing.

Walt Lawson, M.V.: Commented on three items ~ 1) the widening of La Paz Road, between
Chrisanta and the 5 freeway; 2) the safety of bikes and E-bikes in the City; and 3) Consent Calendar
Item #13, Ordinance 23-349, pertaining to Commission term limits and nepotism.

Peggy O’Neill, M.V.: Spoke on voting rights and how hers was denied. She shared her upset on
how three council members unlawfully extending their terms in office last year.

Tom Moore, M.V.: Expressed his concern of the Urban Core Vision Plan and suggested funds go
to a specific plan for this area. He also requested Consent Calendar Item #13, Ordinance 23-349
be pulled for discussion.

Robert Breton, M.V.: Spoke of his pride and satisfaction of Mission Viejo, however he added the
City is recreation rich and cultural arts poor. He stated the time has come to build a 300-400 seat
performing arts center, and thanked the Council for their enthusiastic support.

City Council Minutes  2  February 14, 2023
 Cathy Kadison, M.V.: Reference the nepotism policy adopted in 1989 for City staff and questioned
why it is not appropriate for elected officials as well?

Lynne Hayes, M.V.: Referred to the January 10, 2023, City Council meeting, the selection of
elected official appointments, and remarked on Mayor Pro Tem Kelley and Council Member
Ruesch’s comments on Commission term limits and nepotism.

Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Acknowledged Bob Breton’s work in establishing the City’s Library. She
also voiced her concerns regarding Consent Calendar Item #13, Ordinance 23-349, and stated it
should be pulled from the consent calendar. Lastly, she questioned why should the same policy
not apply to council and commission that applies to staff.

City Council Minutes  7  February 14, 2023
 Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum thanked Congresswoman Young Kim and her team for attending this
evenings Council meeting. She thanked and gave a special welcome to Kim Carr with Senator
Blackspear’s Office, and thanked County Supervisor Don Wagner’s representative for supporting
those being honored today. Council Member Bucknum gave an update on the roundtable for South
Orange County Sober Living Task Force, which has received much interest from other cities. She
asked Dennis Wilberg to elaborate on the City Managers Task Force Group. Dennis mentioned
that he, together with the City Manager of Costa Mesa are setting up a working group to support
the efforts of Council Member Bucknum’s Task Force Group, and also working with various
legislator representatives. He added, the City has filed an amicus brief with the cities of Newport
Beach, Orange, and Fountain Valley in support of Costa Mesa and their continuing fight to uphold
their sober living ordinance. Council Member Bucknum spoke briefly of appointments, and
mentioned that in her first year on the City Counil she did not receive an appointment, however,
she now serves on SCAG and OCCOG. Lastly, with regards to term limits and nepotism, Council
Member Bucknum stated everyone has a choice, and she will not be appointing someone who is
related to someone else, and will seek to appoint people that have not termed out.

Council Member Ruesch

Council Member Ruesch gave a brief history of the Garden Plaza Project during his time as a
Planning and Transportation Commissioner. He stated that the owners approached him again, and
presented a new plan to City Staff. In the interest of transparency, he informed the owners that he
represents District 1 and Mission Viejo, and that before they start any project, he suggested they
meet with the residents of Mission Viejo. Council Member Ruesch added that he had the
opportunity of touring the amazing OCFA facility, and he looks forward to working on the OCFA
Board. As the Vector Control Trustee, he summarized his three-day Vector Control Seminar.
Council Member Ruesch reported that he participated in the Gnome Hunt at the Oso Creek Golf
Course, which was well attended. He also attended the Sensory-friendly Concert and gave kudos
to Director of Library and Cultural Services Genesis Hansen for putting on a fantastic program,
plus he attended a number of Chamber Mixers. He concluded his report by stating that he and
Council Member Vazquez attended the three-day League of California Cities (LOCC) 2023 New
Mayors and Council Members Academy.

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez stated that she attended the Orange County Housing Finance Trust
(OCHFT) meeting and will provide a report at the next Council meting. She recently toured the
Felipe, Montanoso, and Sierra Recreation Facilities, and commented on the great renovations and
great places to hold affordable smaller parties. She also met with Kim Carr of Senator Blackspear’s
Office, and spoke of collaborating on different events together, with a particular interest in the
non-profits that the city partners with, specifically women and military. Council Member Vasquez
also met with the Principal at Capo Valley High School, to introduce herself and see how the City
can be of assistance. A possibility would be the existing traffic situation. She also attended the
League of California Cities (LOCC) Academy, which was a great opportunity to make connections
with other Council Members from all over the state. She attended the Garden+Grille opening at
the Oso Creek Golf Course. And lastly, this morning she met with the Principal at Carl Hankey
City Council Minutes  8  February 14, 2023
 Elementary School, who mentioned that she would be interested in bringing back the tutoring
program at Felipe Tennis Center.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that she and Mayor Goodell met with Congresswoman Young
Kim prior to this evening’s meeting, and stated that she has an office here at City Hall on the
second floor. She added, that if any high school/college students are interested in an internship
they should contact the Congresswoman’s Office. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley also clarified, that the
reason an OCFA alternate is not appointed, is because the State legislature took that privileged
away a number of years ago. She mentioned that she has resumed taking her grandchildren to
Storytime, and thanked Director of Library and Cultural Services Genesis Hansen and her staff for
moving the program back to the wonderful Storytime room. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley congratulated
the Employees of the Year. Bryan Zahn for the City, Fire Captain Danny Goodwin for OCFA, and
Crime Prevention Specialist Timory McElwain for OCSD. She concluded by stating the Character
word for this month is Unity, and encourage all to attend the film of character Hidden Figures for
this month on Sunday, February 19, at 1pm in the Council Chamber.

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell stated that he also attended the meeting with Congresswoman Young Kim today,
and added that he is excited that she and her staff have an office at City Hall. He also met with
Senator Blakespear on Friday, and surprisingly only Kim Carr, and Esther Sanchez the Mayor of
Oceanside were on the zoom call with him. He mentioned that he appreciated the time with the
Senator and looks forward to forging a closer relationship, working on solving issues, in particular
the Sober Living Task Force. He referenced a number of upcoming meetings he has, Orange
County Transportation Authority (OCTA), Orange County Council of Governments (OCCOG),
Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG), and commented on the important of
participating on these boards, and letting our voice be heard and opinions be known on a regional
basis. Mayor Goodell concluded by stating the City is well represented on OCCOG, SCAG,
OCTA, OCFA, OCHFT and the Southern Orange County Watershed Management Area Executive
Committee, as the Council continue to work and be the voice of community.
